title: KV cache compaction canary rollout checklist (Hosted + Dedicated)
content:
Purpose
This is the step-by-step canary enablement checklist for the KV cache compaction + eviction changes in the serving runtime. The goal is to safely validate tail latency, allocator stability, and OOM risk improvements in a controlled slice (one Hosted region/pool + one Dedicated pool) before ramping.

Scope
- Applies to runtime builds that include the compaction feature flag and compaction budgeting.
- Canary targets:
  1) Hosted: us-east-1 / pool: hosted-gpu-a100-1 (low blast radius, high traffic diversity)
  2) Dedicated: pool: ded-omega-a100 (one consenting customer account; confirm with Product)

Definitions / shorthand
- “Compaction”: moving KV blocks/pages to reduce fragmentation.
- “Eviction”: dropping KV state per policy when under pressure.
- “Allocator failures”: allocation failure counter increases (not necessarily OOM, but a strong leading indicator).
- “Fragmentation ratio”: allocator-reported fragmentation metric (see KV cache health dashboard).

Owners & comms channels
- Rollout owner (SRE): Sean Gallagher
- Runtime oncall: (rotate) — ensure assigned in PagerDuty before start
- Release train: Connor O’Brien
- Runtime eng point: Omar El-Sayed (allocator/compaction), Sofia Ivanova (scheduler integration)
- Observability: Allison Grant

Primary channels:
- #eng-sre (rollout coordination)
- #eng-runtime (runtime questions / config)
- #incidents (if any rollback / incident declared)
- #eng-releases (build/version coordination)
- Dedicated customer comms: via PM/CS thread (do not post customer-identifying details in public channels)


SECTION 0 — Pre-flight (T-3 to T-1 days)
[ ] Confirm runtime version / build SHA that contains:
    - feature flag plumbing (PR-18469)
    - allocator metrics (PR-18423)
    - compaction engine + race fixes (PR-18457, PR-18490)
    - perf-canary gate updated (perf-canary PR-388)
[ ] Confirm feature flag default is OFF globally.
[ ] Confirm configs are present in the runtime config registry (names below) and show up in config dump for a canary host.
[ ] Confirm dashboards exist and are populated in staging AND prod:
    - KV Cache Health Dashboard (pool/region breakdown)
    - Hosted Tail Latency dashboard (p95/p99 per route + model family)
    - GPU memory / OOM dashboard for canary pools
    - Scheduler health (queue depth, admission control drops, backpressure signals)
[ ] Confirm alerts are defined but set to “notify only” during first 2 hours of canary (no paging), then normal paging.
[ ] Confirm rollback mechanism:
    - ability to disable flag at pool level (no redeploy)
    - ability to set budget to 0 (soft-disable) if needed
    - ability to revert eviction mode to baseline
[ ] Confirm runbook is up-to-date: Confluence runbook “Mitigating KV cache fragmentation incidents”.
[ ] Confirm perf baseline / acceptance criteria are agreed (see Section 2) and posted in #eng-sre.
[ ] Confirm canary window and staffing:
    - 2-hour “active watch” period must overlap with Runtime oncall + SRE on shift
    - release engineer available for quick hotfix/backport decision

Recommended initial flag values (starting point)
- kv.compaction.enabled = true (ONLY in canary pools)
- kv.compaction.trigger.fragmentation_ratio = 0.25
- kv.compaction.trigger.on_alloc_failure = true
- kv.compaction.budget.ms_per_interval = 2 (interval = 1000ms)
- kv.compaction.budget.max_bytes_per_interval = 256MB (guardrail)
- kv.eviction.mode = "tiered_fair_v1" (if applicable; otherwise baseline)
- scheduler.cache_pressure.enabled = true (canary only)

NOTE: exact config keys may differ by runtime; use config dump as source of truth and update this doc if keys renamed.


SECTION 1 — Launch day checklist (T-0)
1.1 Change management
[ ] Create a short rollout thread in #eng-sre with:
    - start time, expected duration
    - canary targets (pool + region)
    - runtime version
    - rollback plan summary
    - links: dashboards + runbook + this checklist
[ ] Announce in #eng-runtime that canary is starting; request eyes on allocator + scheduler signals for first 2 hours.
[ ] For Dedicated pool: confirm with Product (Lauren Bishop) + CS on the day that the account is still OK with canary; confirm they know how to reach us.

1.2 Confirm steady state before any changes (baseline capture)
[ ] Snapshot the following (paste into rollout thread):
    - p95/p99 end-to-end latency for top 5 routes (Hosted) in the canary region/pool
    - allocator fragmentation ratio (avg + p95) for canary pool
    - allocation failure rate (per min)
    - eviction rate (per min) and top reasons
    - GPU memory utilization (avg/p95) and any OOM events in last 24h
    - admission control drops / queue depth
    - compaction counters should be ZERO (since flag is off)
[ ] Confirm there is no ongoing incident and no abnormal traffic event (product launch / known load test) that would confound results.

1.3 Enable canary (Hosted first)
[ ] Step A: Enable kv.compaction.enabled for Hosted canary pool ONLY.
[ ] Step B: Enable scheduler cache-pressure coordination for the same pool (if separate flag).
[ ] Step C: Start with conservative budgets (see recommended values). Do NOT start with aggressive budgets.
[ ] Verify runtime config propagation:
    - check 2–3 hosts in the pool to ensure config is applied
    - confirm metrics now include compaction counters (even if near-zero initially)

1.4 Hold and observe (first 30–60 minutes)
[ ] Watch dashboards (see Section 3) focusing on early regressions:
    - median latency should not increase materially
    - p99 should not spike relative to baseline
    - allocation failures should not increase
    - GPU memory should remain stable
[ ] Check for log patterns:
    - repeated compaction triggers (thrash)
    - frequent “on_alloc_failure” compaction events
    - any warnings about stream sync / in-flight kernels
[ ] If stable after 60 minutes, proceed to Dedicated pool enablement.

1.5 Enable canary (Dedicated)
[ ] Confirm dedicated pool name and routing are correct (do not affect non-target pools).
[ ] Apply same flags/budgets as Hosted unless the pool has distinct workload (long-context heavy).
[ ] Notify Product/CS that Dedicated canary is enabled and we’re in watch window.


SECTION 2 — Success criteria (what “good” looks like)
Primary (must-have)
- Allocation failures: no sustained increase; target reduction under burst scenarios.
- OOM events: no increase vs baseline (ideally decreases due to reduced fragmentation pressure).
- Tail latency (p95/p99): no regression; target measurable p99 improvement during bursty periods.

Secondary (nice-to-have)
- Fragmentation ratio: downward shift (lower average and fewer high-percentile spikes).
- Eviction churn: reduction in eviction/alloc cycles per request during mixed-length traffic.
- Scheduler health: fewer admission-control drops attributable to cache pressure; reduced queue spikes.

Quantitative gates (initial canary; tune after first 24h)
- Hard gate (rollback immediately):
  - p99 latency +10% sustained for >10 minutes for any major route/model family in canary pool
  - allocation failure rate > baseline + 2x sustained for >5 minutes
  - any new reproducible correctness issue (corruption, crashes) correlated with compaction
  - OOM events increase (>=2 events) within 1 hour where none existed in baseline window
- Soft gate (pause / tune budgets):
  - median latency +3–5% sustained (compaction overhead too high)
  - compaction time/cost metrics show repeated max-budget hits each interval (indicates thrash)
  - eviction rate increases significantly without corresponding reduction in tail latency


SECTION 3 — Dashboards to watch (during active watch + 24h)
Core: KV Cache Health Dashboard (filter by region + pool)
- Fragmentation ratio (avg/p95/p99)
- Allocation failures (count/min)
- Compaction events (count/min)
- Bytes moved (per min; and per interval if available)
- Compaction time (CPU/GPU time; if broken out)
- Eviction rate + eviction reasons (tier, age, pressure)

Latency & SLO dashboards
- Hosted tail latency: p95/p99 by route, model family, and pool
- Dedicated account view: p95/p99 per deployment; timeouts / error rate
- Error budgets: check that SLO burn rate is not increasing in canary pools

Infra / runtime health
- GPU memory utilization + fragmentation (if available at driver layer)
- Runtime restarts / crash loops
- Scheduler: queue depth, backpressure signals, admission-control drops

Perf-canary gating
- Confirm new perf-canary scenario is green for compaction-enabled build.
- If perf-canary fails but production looks OK, treat as “pause” and investigate; do not ramp until understood.


SECTION 4 — Rollback plan (fast path)
Rollback triggers: use Section 2 gates.

Rollback steps (in order)
[ ] Step 1 (fastest): set kv.compaction.enabled = false for the impacted pool(s).
[ ] Step 2: if disable propagation is slow or partial, set kv.compaction.budget.ms_per_interval = 0 (soft-disable) and leave enabled flag unchanged temporarily.
[ ] Step 3: revert eviction mode to baseline (kv.eviction.mode = "baseline") if eviction interaction is suspected.
[ ] Step 4: disable scheduler cache-pressure integration if it’s causing throughput collapse or starvation.
[ ] Step 5: if issues persist (crash/corruption), coordinate with Release to roll back runtime version for the pool.

Rollback verification
[ ] Confirm compaction counters flatten (no new compaction events after change).
[ ] Confirm latency returns to baseline within 10–20 minutes.
[ ] Confirm allocation failure rate returns to baseline.
[ ] Post an update in #eng-sre and #eng-runtime with what was rolled back and why.
[ ] If customer-visible impact occurred, notify PM/CS with a short incident-style summary and next steps.

Escalation
- Page Runtime oncall if any correctness signal or repeated crashes.
- Declare incident if customer timeouts/SLO breach is ongoing and not resolved within 15 minutes.


SECTION 5 — Ramp plan (after first 24 hours)
If canary is healthy for 24 hours:
[ ] Post a 24h summary in #eng-sre:
    - p95/p99 deltas, allocation failures, OOM count, fragmentation ratio shift
    - any tuning performed (budgets/thresholds)
    - open issues / follow-ups
[ ] Proceed to next ramp stage (per Linear ENG-2852):
    - Hosted: 5% of pools in us-east-1 OR 25% of traffic in the canary pool (choose one consistent lever)
    - Dedicated: add 1 additional consenting pool/account
[ ] Ensure alerts switch from “notify only” to paging for the new blast radius.

Tuning guidance (only change one dimension at a time)
- If p99 improved but median regressed: lower compaction budget (ms_per_interval) and/or raise fragmentation trigger.
- If allocation failures still occur: allow “on_alloc_failure” compaction, slightly increase byte budget, but monitor median.
- If eviction spikes: verify scheduler cache-pressure contract; consider adjusting victim selection weights.


SECTION 6 — Communications plan
Internal comms
- Start-of-canary message (in #eng-sre) must include:
  - targets, version, flags, dashboards, rollback triggers
- Any config tuning during canary:
  - post exact key/value changes and timestamp
- End-of-day summary:
  - what we saw, whether continuing overnight, who is watching

Customer-facing comms (Dedicated)
- PM/CS should message the customer that:
  - change is runtime-only (no API behavior change expected)
  - we’re validating latency stability improvements
  - rollback is immediate if any degradation occurs
- If there is a regression:
  - acknowledge, roll back, and provide timeline for follow-up (do not speculate on root cause until confirmed)


SECTION 7 — Notes / open questions
- Confirm final names for config keys (update this doc once merged into the runtime config docs).
- Decide whether we want a separate canary for long-context-heavy pools (risk: compaction bandwidth + stream sync overhead).
- Ensure we have per-request attribution for “latency impacted by compaction” (useful for post-analysis and customer narratives).

Change log
- 2025-02-18: initial draft (Sean)
- 2025-03-05: added explicit gates and budget tuning guidance; added Dedicated comms steps (Sean, Rafael, Allison)
